236	
237	Questions? Open a discussion or reach out to the maintainers.

1	# intropy CLI
2	
3	`intropy` is the command-line interface for working with Intropy integrations.
4	It **scaffolds integrations** from the official Intropy blueprint library hosted at
5	[`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints).
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)
10	
11	```sh
12	brew tap intropy/tap
13	brew install intropy
14	```
15	
16	### Quick install (macOS / Linux)
17	
18	```sh
19	curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh
20	```
21	
22	With options:
23	
24	```sh
25	# Install to a custom prefix
26	curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --prefix ~/.local
27	
28	# Install a specific version
29	curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.1.0
30	```
31	
32	The script detects your OS and architecture, downloads the matching release
33	archive, verifies the SHA256 checksum, optionally verifies the cosign signature,
34	and installs the binary and shell completions.
35	
36	### From source
37	
38	Requires Go 1.26+.
39	
40	```sh
41	git clone https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli.git
42	cd intropy-cli
43	make build
44	```
45	
46	Or manually:
47	
48	```sh
49	go build -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
50	```
51	
52	Add `bin/` to your `PATH`, or move the binary somewhere on your `PATH`.
53	
54	### Verifying signatures
55	
56	Release binaries are signed with [cosign](https://sigstore.dev/) using
57	keyless signing via GitHub Actions OIDC. Each release includes `.sig` and
58	`.pem` files for every archive.
59	
60	```sh
61	# Download the archive, its .sig, and its .pem from the GitHub release
62	cosign verify-blob \
63	  --certificate intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.pem \
64	  --signature intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.sig \
65	  --certificate-identity-regexp="https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli" \
66	  --certificate-oidc-issuer="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
67	  intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
68	```
69	
70	### Windows
71	
72	Windows is not a supported native target. Install and run `intropy` inside
73	[WSL 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) using the Linux
74	instructions above. The CLI relies on Unix path conventions and signal handling
75	that are not tested on Windows.
76	
77	### Version stamping
78	
79	Version, commit, and build date are injected via `-ldflags` at release time:
80	
81	```sh
82	go build -ldflags "\
83	  -X main.version=$(git describe --tags --always) \
84	  -X main.commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
85	  -X main.date=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
86	  -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
87	```
88	
89	Check what you have with:
90	
91	```sh
92	intropy version
93	```
94	
95	## Quickstart
96	
97	### Scaffold your first integration
98	
99	```sh
100	# Inspect a blueprint before you scaffold it
101	intropy int describe hello-world
102	
103	# Render it into a new directory
104	intropy int create hello-world -o ./my-integration
105	```
106	
107	## Command overview
108	
109	```
110	intropy
111	├── int                    Manage integrations
112	│   ├── create <blueprint>     Scaffold a new integration from a blueprint
113	│   └── describe <blueprint>   Print a blueprint's manifest and parameter schema
114	└── version                Print version information
115	```
116	
117	Run any command with `--help` for full flag documentation.
118	
119	## Integrations (`intropy int`)
120	
121	### Describe a blueprint
122	
123	Inspect what parameters a blueprint accepts before scaffolding it:
124	
125	```sh
126	intropy int describe hello-world
127	intropy int describe hello-world --version v1.2.0
128	intropy int describe hello-world -o json   # machine-readable; same schema Backstage renders
129	```
130	
131	Without `--version`, the latest GitHub release is used.
132	
133	### Create an integration
134	
135	```sh
136	intropy int create hello-world --output ./my-integration
137	```
138	
139	Provide parameter values inline, from files, or interactively:
140	
141	```sh
142	# inline
143	intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --set name=orders --set owner=team-x
144	
145	# from a values file (repeatable; use - for stdin)
146	intropy int create hello-world -o ./out -f values.yaml
147	
148	# disable interactive prompts (fail fast on missing required values)
149	intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --no-input -f values.yaml
150	
151	# write a machine-readable result document (consumed by chained scaffolders)
152	intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --output-json result.json
153	```
154	
155	Use `--force` to render into a non-empty directory.
156	
157	## Project layout
158	
159	```
160	cmd/intropy/         Cobra command wiring (one file per command)
161	internal/blueprint/  Blueprint download, validation, describe, render
162	```
163	
164	## Exit codes
165	
166	- `0` — success
167	- `1` — runtime error
168	- `2` — usage error (unknown command, missing required flag, bad argument)
169	
170	## Troubleshooting
171	
172	| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
173	|---------|-------|-----|
174	| `intropy int create` fails with "blueprint not found" | The blueprint name is misspelled or does not exist in the library. | Run `intropy int describe <name>` to verify the blueprint exists. Check spelling and case. |
175	| Windows native errors | Running the Linux binary directly on Windows without WSL. | Use WSL 2 — native Windows is not supported. |
176	
177	For issues not listed here, run the failing command with `--help` to verify flag usage, or open an issue with the output of `intropy version` and the exact command you ran.
178	
179	## Contributing
180	
181	See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for build instructions, code standards,
182	and the pull request workflow.
183	
184	## References
185	
186	- [`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints)
187	  — the blueprint library `intropy int create` and `intropy int describe`
188	  download from by default.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# intropy CLI

`intropy` is the command-line interface for working with Intropy integrations.
It **scaffolds integrations** from the official Intropy blueprint library hosted at
[`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints).

## Install

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew tap intropy/tap
brew install intropy
```

### Quick install (macOS / Linux)

```sh
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh
```

With options:

```sh
# Install to a custom prefix
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --prefix ~/.local

# Install a specific version
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.1.0
```

The script detects your OS and architecture, downloads the matching release
archive, verifies the SHA256 checksum, optionally verifies the cosign signature,
and installs the binary and shell completions.

### From source

Requires Go 1.26+.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli.git
cd intropy-cli
make build
```

Or manually:

```sh
go build -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
```

Add `bin/` to your `PATH`, or move the binary somewhere on your `PATH`.

### Verifying signatures

Release binaries are signed with [cosign](https://sigstore.dev/) using
keyless signing via GitHub Actions OIDC. Each release includes `.sig` and
`.pem` files for every archive.

```sh
# Download the archive, its .sig, and its .pem from the GitHub release
cosign verify-blob \
  --certificate intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.pem \
  --signature intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.sig \
  --certificate-identity-regexp="https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
```

### Windows

Windows is not a supported native target. Install and run `intropy` inside
[WSL 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) using the Linux
instructions above. The CLI relies on Unix path conventions and signal handling
that are not tested on Windows.

### Version stamping

Version, commit, and build date are injected via `-ldflags` at release time:

```sh
go build -ldflags "\
  -X main.version=$(git describe --tags --always) \
  -X main.commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
  -X main.date=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
  -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
```

Check what you have with:

```sh
intropy version
```

## Quickstart

### Scaffold your first integration

```sh
# Inspect a blueprint before you scaffold it
intropy int describe hello-world

# Render it into a new directory
intropy int create hello-world -o ./my-integration
```

## Command overview

```
intropy
├── int                    Manage integrations
│   ├── create <blueprint>     Scaffold a new integration from a blueprint
│   └── describe <blueprint>   Print a blueprint's manifest and parameter schema
└── version                Print version information
```

Run any command with `--help` for full flag documentation.

## Integrations (`intropy int`)

### Describe a blueprint

Inspect what parameters a blueprint accepts before scaffolding it:

```sh
intropy int describe hello-world
intropy int describe hello-world --version v1.2.0
intropy int describe hello-world -o json   # machine-readable; same schema Backstage renders
```

Without `--version`, the latest GitHub release is used.

### Create an integration

```sh
intropy int create hello-world --output ./my-integration
```

Provide parameter values inline, from files, or interactively:

```sh
# inline
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --set name=orders --set owner=team-x

# from a values file (repeatable; use - for stdin)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out -f values.yaml

# disable interactive prompts (fail fast on missing required values)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --no-input -f values.yaml

# write a machine-readable result document (consumed by chained scaffolders)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --output-json result.json
```

Use `--force` to render into a non-empty directory.

## Project layout

```
cmd/intropy/         Cobra command wiring (one file per command)
internal/blueprint/  Blueprint download, validation, describe, render
```

## Exit codes

- `0` — success
- `1` — runtime error
- `2` — usage error (unknown command, missing required flag, bad argument)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `intropy int create` fails with "blueprint not found" | The blueprint name is misspelled or does not exist in the library. | Run `intropy int describe <name>` to verify the blueprint exists. Check spelling and case. |
| Windows native errors | Running the Linux binary directly on Windows without WSL. | Use WSL 2 — native Windows is not supported. |

For issues not listed here, run the failing command with `--help` to verify flag usage, or open an issue with the output of `intropy version` and the exact command you ran.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for build instructions, code standards,
and the pull request workflow.

## References

- [`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints)
  — the blueprint library `intropy int create` and `intropy int describe`
  download from by default.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/bin/sh
# install.sh — install intropy from GitHub Releases
#
# Usage:
#   curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh
#   curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.1.0
#   curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --prefix ~/.local

set -e

OWNER="intropy"
REPO="intropy-cli"
BINARY="intropy"
GITHUB="https://github.com/${OWNER}/${REPO}"

# Defaults
PREFIX=""
VERSION=""

# Parse arguments passed via sh -s -- ...
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
	case "$1" in
		--version)
			VERSION="$2"
			shift 2
			;;
		--prefix)
			PREFIX="$2"
			shift 2
			;;
		-h|--help)
			echo "Usage: install.sh [--version VERSION] [--prefix PREFIX]"
			echo ""
			echo "Options:"
			echo "  --version VERSION   Install a specific version (default: latest)"
			echo "  --prefix PREFIX     Install directory (default: /usr/local/bin or ~/.local/bin)"
			exit 0
			;;
		*)
			echo "Unknown option: $1"
			exit 1
			;;
	esac
done

# --- detect OS ---
OS=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
case "$OS" in
	linux) OS="Linux" ;;
	darwin) OS="Darwin" ;;
	*)
		echo "Unsupported operating system: $OS"
		echo "Supported: Linux, Darwin (macOS)"
		exit 1
		;;
esac

# --- detect architecture ---
ARCH=$(uname -m)
case "$ARCH" in
	x86_64) ARCH="amd64" ;;
	aarch64|arm64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
	*)
		echo "Unsupported architecture: $ARCH"
		echo "Supported: amd64, arm64"
		exit 1
		;;
esac

# --- resolve version ---
if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
	# Fetch the latest release tag from GitHub API
	echo "==> Resolving latest version..."
	VERSION=$(curl -fsSL "${GITHUB}/releases/latest" | sed -n 's/.*tag_name":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
	if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
		echo "Failed to determine latest version"
		exit 1
	fi
fi

echo "==> Installing ${BINARY} ${VERSION} for ${OS}/${ARCH}..."

# --- determine install directory ---
if [ -z "$PREFIX" ]; then
	# Try /usr/local/bin first, fall back to ~/.local/bin
	if [ -w "/usr/local/bin" ] 2>/dev/null || mkdir -p "/usr/local/bin" 2>/dev/null; then
		PREFIX="/usr/local/bin"
	else
		PREFIX="${HOME}/.local/bin"
		mkdir -p "$PREFIX"
	fi
fi

if [ ! -d "$PREFIX" ]; then
	mkdir -p "$PREFIX" || {
		echo "Failed to create directory: $PREFIX"
		exit 1
	}
fi

echo "==> Install directory: $PREFIX"

# --- download artifact ---
ARTIFACT="${BINARY}_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR"' EXIT

BASE_URL="${GITHUB}/releases/download/${VERSION}"

echo "==> Downloading ${ARTIFACT}..."
curl -fsSL "${BASE_URL}/${ARTIFACT}" -o "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}"

# --- download and verify checksum ---
echo "==> Verifying checksum..."
curl -fsSL "${BASE_URL}/checksums.txt" -o "${TMPDIR}/checksums.txt"
cd "$TMPDIR"

# Extract the expected checksum for our artifact
EXPECTED=$(grep "${ARTIFACT}" checksums.txt | awk '{print $1}')
if [ -z "$EXPECTED" ]; then
	echo "Artifact not found in checksums.txt"
	exit 1
fi

# Compute actual checksum
ACTUAL=$(sha256sum "${ARTIFACT}" | awk '{print $1}')
if [ "$EXPECTED" != "$ACTUAL" ]; then
	echo "Checksum mismatch!"
	echo "  expected: ${EXPECTED}"
	echo "  actual:   ${ACTUAL}"
	exit 1
fi

echo "==> Checksum OK"

# --- optional cosign verification ---
if command -v cosign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo "==> Verifying signature with cosign..."
	curl -fsSL "${BASE_URL}/${ARTIFACT}.sig" -o "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}.sig"
	curl -fsSL "${BASE_URL}/${ARTIFACT}.pem" -o "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}.pem"
	cosign verify-blob \
		--certificate "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}.pem" \
		--signature "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}.sig" \
		--certificate-identity-regexp="https://github.com/${OWNER}/${REPO}" \
		--certificate-oidc-issuer="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
		"${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}" || {
		echo "Cosign verification failed"
		exit 1
	}
	echo "==> Signature verified"
else
	echo "==> cosign not found, skipping signature verification"
	echo "    (install cosign to verify: https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/installation/)"
fi

# --- extract and install ---
echo "==> Extracting..."
tar -xzf "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}" -C "$TMPDIR"

# The binary should be at TMPDIR/intropy or TMPDIR/bin/intropy
if [ -f "${TMPDIR}/${BINARY}" ]; then
	BINARY_PATH="${TMPDIR}/${BINARY}"
elif [ -f "${TMPDIR}/bin/${BINARY}" ]; then
	BINARY_PATH="${TMPDIR}/bin/${BINARY}"
else
	echo "Binary not found in archive"
	exit 1
fi

echo "==> Installing ${BINARY} to ${PREFIX}..."
if [ -w "$PREFIX" ]; then
	install -m 755 "$BINARY_PATH" "${PREFIX}/${BINARY}"
else
	echo "    (sudo required for ${PREFIX})"
	sudo install -m 755 "$BINARY_PATH" "${PREFIX}/${BINARY}"
fi

# --- install shell completions ---
if command -v "${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo "==> Installing shell completions..."

	# Bash
	if [ -d "/etc/bash_completion.d" ] && [ -w "/etc/bash_completion.d" ]; then
		"${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" completion bash > "/etc/bash_completion.d/${BINARY}"
		echo "    bash: /etc/bash_completion.d/${BINARY}"
	elif [ -d "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d" ] && [ -w "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d" ]; then
		"${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" completion bash > "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/${BINARY}"
		echo "    bash: /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/${BINARY}"
	fi

	# Zsh
	if [ -d "/usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions" ] && [ -w "/usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions" ]; then
		"${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" completion zsh > "/usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_${BINARY}"
		echo "    zsh: /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_${BINARY}"
	elif [ -d "${HOME}/.zsh/completions" ]; then
		mkdir -p "${HOME}/.zsh/completions"
		"${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" completion zsh > "${HOME}/.zsh/completions/_${BINARY}"
		echo "    zsh: ~/.zsh/completions/_${BINARY}"
	fi

	# Fish
	if [ -d "${HOME}/.config/fish/completions" ]; then
		mkdir -p "${HOME}/.config/fish/completions"
		"${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" completion fish > "${HOME}/.config/fish/completions/${BINARY}.fish"
		echo "    fish: ~/.config/fish/completions/${BINARY}.fish"
	fi
fi

# --- verify installation ---
echo ""
echo "==> ${BINARY} installed successfully!"
"${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" version

# --- PATH warning ---
case ":${PATH}:" in
	*":${PREFIX}:"*) ;;
	*)
		echo ""
		echo "WARNING: ${PREFIX} is not in your PATH."
		echo "Add the following to your shell profile:"
		echo "  export PATH=\"${PREFIX}:\${PATH}\""
		;;
esac

# GoReleaser configuration for intropy CLI
# https://goreleaser.com/
#
# Usage:
#   goreleaser release --clean        # full release (requires GITHUB_TOKEN)
#   goreleaser release --snapshot     # test build without publishing

version: 2

project_name: intropy

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy
    - go test ./...

builds:
  - id: intropy
    main: ./cmd/intropy
    binary: intropy
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - linux
      - darwin
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X main.version={{.Version}}
      - -X main.commit={{.Commit}}
      - -X main.date={{.Date}}
    flags:
      - -trimpath

archives:
  - format: tar.gz
    name_template: >-
      {{ .ProjectName }}_
      {{- .Version }}_
      {{- .Os }}_
      {{- .Arch }}
    files:
      - README.md
      - LICENSE
      - CONTRIBUTING.md
      - install.sh

signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    certificate: '${artifact}.pem'
    args:
      - sign-blob
      - '--output-certificate=${certificate}'
      - '--output-signature=${signature}'
      - '${artifact}'
    artifacts: all

checksum:
  name_template: checksums.txt
  algorithm: sha256

snapshot:
  version_template: "{{ incpatch .Version }}-rc"

changelog:
  sort: asc
  use: github
  filters:
    exclude:
      - '^docs:'
      - '^test:'
      - '^chore:'
      - Merge pull request
      - Merge branch
  groups:
    - title: Features
      regexp: '^.*?feat(\(.+\))?!?:.*$'
      order: 0
    - title: Bug Fixes
      regexp: '^.*?fix(\(.+\))?!?:.*$'
      order: 1
    - title: Other Changes
      order: 999

brews:
  - name: intropy
    repository:
      owner: integrio-intropy
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Formula
    homepage: "https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli"
    description: "CLI for Intropy integrations"
    license: "MIT"
    test: |
      system "#{bin}/intropy", "version"
    install: |
      bin.install "intropy"
      output = Utils.safe_popen_read(bin/"intropy", "completion", "bash")
      (bash_completion/"intropy").write output
      output = Utils.safe_popen_read(bin/"intropy", "completion", "zsh")
      (zsh_completion/"_intropy").write output
      output = Utils.safe_popen_read(bin/"intropy", "completion", "fish")
      (fish_completion/"intropy.fish").write output
    dependencies:
      - name: cosign
        type: optional

release:
  github:
    owner: integrio-intropy
    name: intropy-cli
  draft: true
  prerelease: auto
  extra_files:
    - glob: ./install.sh

name: release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*'

permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write   # required for cosign keyless signing via OIDC

jobs:
  goreleaser:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      - name: Verify tag matches go.mod
        run: |
          TAG="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}"
          echo "Tag: $TAG"

      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
        with:
          cosign-release: 'v2.4.1'

      - uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v6
        with:
          version: '~> v2'
          args: release --clean
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

**Yes, the code is.** It's already on `origin/main`. Builds, vet, gofmt, and `go test ./...` all pass (the release pipeline runs tests via a `before` hook, so deferring *additional* tests is fine — existing ones pass). cosign signing is keyless via OIDC, already wired in the workflow with `id-token: write`.

| # | Item | Status |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | Tap repo `integrio-intropy/homebrew-tap` exists | ✅ exists — **but PRIVATE** ⚠️ |
| 2 | `TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret on `intropy-cli` | ❌ **not set** (blocker) |

**Two things block / break a Homebrew release:**

1. **`TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN` is missing.** GoReleaser pushes the generated `Formula/intropy.rb` into the *separate* tap repo, which the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't write to. You need a PAT with write access to `homebrew-tap`:

2. **The tap repo is private.** `brew tap integrio-intropy/tap` / `brew install` will fail for anyone without repo access. If this CLI is for outside users, **make `homebrew-tap` public**. (If it's intentionally internal-only, leave it — users just need to be authenticated.)

## Cutting the release
Once #1 (and #2 if needed) are done:
```sh
git tag v1.0.0
git push origin v1.0.0          # matches v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+* → triggers release.yaml
```
The workflow runs GoReleaser, which builds linux/darwin × amd64/arm64, signs with cosign, commits the formula to the tap, and creates a **draft** GitHub release (`draft: true`). **Final manual step:** open GitHub → Releases and **publish the draft** so the artifacts go public and `brew install` can fetch them.

Then users install with:
```sh
brew install integrio-intropy/tap/intropy
```

## Recommended before tagging (optional but worth it)
Dry-run locally to catch config/build issues without publishing:
```sh
goreleaser check                       # validate config
goreleaser release --snapshot --clean  # full build, no publish
```

message.content: For TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN do I need a personal token or can we use something else?

content.text:
Short answer: **the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` won't work here**, because the formula gets pushed to a *different* repo (`homebrew-tap`), and the Actions-provided `GITHUB_TOKEN` is scoped to only the repo running the workflow. So you need *some* cross-repo write credential — but it doesn't have to be a personal PAT. Options, best to most expedient:

## Options

**1. GitHub App token (best for an org)**
Create a small GitHub App (Contents: Read & write), install it on `homebrew-tap`, and mint a short-lived token at runtime with `actions/create-github-app-token`. Then pass that to `TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- ✅ Not tied to a person (survives someone leaving), least-privilege, auto-expiring tokens, org-managed.
- ➖ ~10 min more setup than a PAT.

**2. Fine-grained PAT (simplest that's still safe)**
A fine-grained personal token scoped to **only** `integrio-intropy/homebrew-tap`, permission **Contents: Read and write**.
- ✅ Quick, narrowly scoped.
- ➖ Tied to your account; expires and needs rotation.

**3. Bot / service-account PAT**
A dedicated machine user added as a collaborator on the tap, with its own PAT.
- ✅ Decouples from a human account.
- ➖ Another account to manage (seat, 2FA).

**4. Classic PAT** — works (`repo` scope) but grants broad access across all your repos. **Avoid** unless nothing else is viable.

## A different architecture that needs *no* extra token
Point the tap at the **same repo** (`integrio-intropy/intropy-cli`) with a `Formula/` directory instead of a separate `homebrew-tap` repo. Then GoReleaser writes the formula into the project repo, and the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` suffices — no `TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN` at all. Users would `brew install integrio-intropy/intropy-cli/intropy`.
- ➖ It commits formula updates into the main repo on every release, which clutters the clean single-commit history you just set up. Given you care about that, I'd lean against it.

## Recommendation
- If this is an org project you want to be durable: **GitHub App token (#1)**.
- If you just want to ship v1 now with minimal fuss: **fine-grained PAT (#2)** scoped to the tap repo.

Either way it ends up as the `TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN` Actions secret on `intropy-cli`, and the `.goreleaser.yaml` already references it — no code change needed. Want me to add the `actions/create-github-app-token` step to `release.yaml` so it's ready for option #1?

content.content:
# GoReleaser Deprecation Replacements

## archives.format

The deprecated `format` property should be renamed to `formats` and converted to a list:

**Before:**
```yaml
archives:
  - format: zip
```

**After:**
```yaml
archives:
  - formats: ["zip"]
```

Note: The system accepts a single string value (e.g., `formats: zip`), so in most cases you only need to rename the property.

## format_overrides.format

Similarly, within `format_overrides`, rename `format` to `formats`:

**Before:**
```yaml
archives:
  - format_overrides:
      - format: zip
```

**After:**
```yaml
archives:
  - format_overrides:
      - formats: ["zip"]
```

## brews Migration

Yes, the replacement for the deprecated `brews` property is `homebrew_casks`. The documentation states that GoReleaser now provides "a new `homebrew_casks` section" for distributing pre-compiled binaries, moving away from the older formula-based approach.

**Before:**
```yaml
brews:
  - name: foo
    directory: Formulas
```

**After:**
```yaml
homebrew_casks:
  - name: foo
    directory: Casks
```

The migration guidance recommends creating a `tap_migrations.json` file in your tap repository to automatically redirect users from the old Formula to the new Cask during upgrades, then removing the original Formula file.

content.content:
# GoReleaser Homebrew Casks Configuration

## Overview

The `homebrew_casks` section enables publishing macOS applications to Homebrew taps after releasing to GitHub, GitLab, or Gitea. This feature became available in v2.10.

## Platform Limitation

Homebrew Casks are **macOS-only**. They cannot be used for Linux distribution.

## Core Configuration Fields

**Essential metadata:**
- `name` - Cask identifier (defaults to project name)
- `binaries` - Executable names within the cask
- `homepage` - Application website
- `description` - Brief app summary

**Installation sources:**
- `url.template` - Download location with templating support
- `url.verified` - Domain verification (e.g., "github.com/owner/repo/")

**Distribution target:**
- `repository.owner` - Tap repository owner
- `repository.name` - Tap repository name
- `repository.branch` - Git branch (defaults to repository default)
- `directory` - Cask file location within tap (default: "Casks")

## Additional Features

**Shell completions** can be provided via:
- Direct file paths: `completions.bash`, `completions.zsh`, `completions.fish`
- Runtime generation: `generate_completions_from_executable` with subcommand arguments

**Manual pages:**
- `manpages` - Array of man file paths

**Lifecycle customization:**
- `hooks.pre.install` / `hooks.post.install`
- `hooks.pre.uninstall` / `hooks.post.uninstall`
- `uninstall` procedures for cleanup
- `zap` for complete removal including user files

**Dependencies and conflicts:**
- `dependencies` - Required casks/formulas
- `conflicts` - Incompatible casks

## Repository Management

**Standard push:**
- Commits changes directly to specified branch

**Pull requests:**
- `pull_request.enabled` - Create PR instead of direct push
- `pull_request.base` - Target repository/branch for cross-repo PRs
- `pull_request.draft` - Open as draft
- `pull_request.body` - Custom PR description

**Advanced:**
- `git.url` - SSH Git repository URL
- `git.private_key` - Authentication credentials
- `commit_author.name` / `commit_author.email` - Author metadata
- `commit_author.signing` - GPG signing configuration

## Versioned Casks (Pro Feature)

The `alternative_names` field creates multiple cask versions:

```yaml
alternative_names:
  - "myapp@{{ .Major }}.{{ .Minor }}"
```

This allows users to install specific versions like `brew install myapp@1.2`.

## macOS Security Considerations

Applications must be signed/notarized or include post-install hooks removing quarantine attributes. The documentation warns that using `xattr` to bypass Gatekeeper "circumvents macOS security protections" and may become unavailable in future versions.

## Special Handling

**Private repositories** require custom download strategies with authentication tokens deferred to runtime, as Homebrew 5.1.14+ scrubs sensitive environment variables during cask loading.

**Pull request templates** from `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` are automatically appended.

content.content:
# Homebrew Casks YAML Example

Here's a complete, copy-pasteable example for a single CLI binary:

```yaml
homebrew_casks:
  - name: myapp
    binaries:
      - myapp
    
    repository:
      owner: myusername
      name: homebrew-myapp
      token: "{{ .Env.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN }}"
    
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://example.com/"
    description: "A fast CLI tool for doing things"
    
    generate_completions_from_executable:
      executable: "bin/myapp"
      args:
        - completion
      base_name: "myapp"
      shell_parameter_format: cobra
      shells:
        - bash
        - zsh
        - fish
    
    hooks:
      post:
        install: |
          if OS.mac?
            system_command "/usr/bin/xattr", args: ["-dr", "com.apple.quarantine", "#{staged_path}/myapp"]
          end
```

## Key Points

# intropy CLI

`intropy` is the command-line interface for working with Intropy integrations.
It **scaffolds integrations** from the official Intropy blueprint library hosted at
[`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints).

## Install

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew tap integrio-intropy/tap
brew install intropy
```

### Quick install (macOS / Linux)

```sh
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh
```

With options:

```sh
# Install to a custom prefix
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --prefix ~/.local

# Install a specific version
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.1.0
```

The script detects your OS and architecture, downloads the matching release
archive, verifies the SHA256 checksum, optionally verifies the cosign signature,
and installs the binary and shell completions.

### From source

Requires Go 1.26+.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli.git
cd intropy-cli
make build
```

Or manually:

```sh
go build -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
```

Add `bin/` to your `PATH`, or move the binary somewhere on your `PATH`.

### Verifying signatures

Release binaries are signed with [cosign](https://sigstore.dev/) using
keyless signing via GitHub Actions OIDC. Each release includes `.sig` and
`.pem` files for every archive.

```sh
# Download the archive, its .sig, and its .pem from the GitHub release
cosign verify-blob \
  --certificate intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.pem \
  --signature intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.sig \
  --certificate-identity-regexp="https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
```

### Windows

Windows is not a supported native target. Install and run `intropy` inside
[WSL 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) using the Linux
instructions above. The CLI relies on Unix path conventions and signal handling
that are not tested on Windows.

### Version stamping

Version, commit, and build date are injected via `-ldflags` at release time:

```sh
go build -ldflags "\
  -X main.version=$(git describe --tags --always) \
  -X main.commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
  -X main.date=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
  -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
```

Check what you have with:

```sh
intropy version
```

## Quickstart

### Scaffold your first integration

```sh
# Inspect a blueprint before you scaffold it
intropy int describe hello-world

# Render it into a new directory
intropy int create hello-world -o ./my-integration
```

## Command overview

```
intropy
├── int                    Manage integrations
│   ├── create <blueprint>     Scaffold a new integration from a blueprint
│   └── describe <blueprint>   Print a blueprint's manifest and parameter schema
└── version                Print version information
```

Run any command with `--help` for full flag documentation.

## Integrations (`intropy int`)

### Describe a blueprint

Inspect what parameters a blueprint accepts before scaffolding it:

```sh
intropy int describe hello-world
intropy int describe hello-world --version v1.2.0
intropy int describe hello-world -o json   # machine-readable; same schema Backstage renders
```

Without `--version`, the latest GitHub release is used.

### Create an integration

```sh
intropy int create hello-world --output ./my-integration
```

Provide parameter values inline, from files, or interactively:

```sh
# inline
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --set name=orders --set owner=team-x

# from a values file (repeatable; use - for stdin)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out -f values.yaml

# disable interactive prompts (fail fast on missing required values)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --no-input -f values.yaml

# write a machine-readable result document (consumed by chained scaffolders)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --output-json result.json
```

Use `--force` to render into a non-empty directory.

## Project layout

```
cmd/intropy/         Cobra command wiring (one file per command)
internal/blueprint/  Blueprint download, validation, describe, render
```

## Exit codes

- `0` — success
- `1` — runtime error
- `2` — usage error (unknown command, missing required flag, bad argument)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `intropy int create` fails with "blueprint not found" | The blueprint name is misspelled or does not exist in the library. | Run `intropy int describe <name>` to verify the blueprint exists. Check spelling and case. |
| Windows native errors | Running the Linux binary directly on Windows without WSL. | Use WSL 2 — native Windows is not supported. |

For issues not listed here, run the failing command with `--help` to verify flag usage, or open an issue with the output of `intropy version` and the exact command you ran.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for build instructions, code standards,
and the pull request workflow.

## References

- [`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints)
  — the blueprint library `intropy int create` and `intropy int describe`
  download from by default.

content.text:
That failure is purely a **local tooling gap, not a config problem** — `cosign` isn't installed on your Mac, so the signing step can't run. Everything before it (build → archive → checksums) succeeded.

You don't need cosign locally. Two ways forward:

**For local snapshot testing — just skip signing** (what you ran earlier that worked):
```sh
goreleaser release --snapshot --clean --skip=sign
```

**If you want to exercise signing locally too:**
```sh
brew install cosign
```
…but heads-up: your config uses cosign **keyless** signing, so a local run will pop a browser for Sigstore OIDC auth each time — fine for a one-off check, annoying for routine local builds. I'd keep using `--skip=sign` locally.

**Real releases are unaffected.** In CI, `release.yaml` installs cosign via `sigstore/cosign-installer@v3` and grants `id-token: write`, so keyless signing works automatically with no browser and no secret. So:
- Local: `--skip=sign`
- CI (on tag push): signs for real, no action needed from you

Nothing to change in the repo — your earlier clean snapshot already proved the build + cask generation work.

content.text:
Yes — you can run the **entire pipeline end-to-end while everything stays private**, which makes the private repos a perfect staging environment. Private repos support Actions, cosign keyless OIDC works regardless of visibility, and your `TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN` can push to the private tap. The one wrinkle is the final `brew install`, which needs a token to read private assets — covered below.

## Recommended: a throwaway pre-release tag

Your workflow triggers on `v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*`, so a pre-release tag works and `prerelease: auto` will flag it as such:

```sh
git tag v0.0.1-rc.1
git push origin v0.0.1-rc.1
```

This runs the **real** pipeline: build 4 platforms → cosign-sign → create a **draft** GitHub release → push `Casks/intropy.rb` into the private `homebrew-tap`. Watch it with `gh run watch`.

**Verify:**
- The draft release has all `.tar.gz` + `.sig` + `.pem` + `checksums.txt`.
- `homebrew-tap` got `Casks/intropy.rb` with correct `version`, URLs, and sha256s.

## Testing `brew install` while private

Two things to know:
1. GoReleaser makes the release a **draft** — draft assets have no working download URL. So **publish the (pre)release** first. In a private repo it stays private (only collaborators + a token can see it).
2. Then install with a token that can read both private repos:

```sh
export HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN=<PAT with read on intropy-cli + homebrew-tap>
brew install integrio-intropy/tap/intropy
intropy version
```

## Clean up before the real launch (so v1.0.0 is pristine)

```sh
gh release delete v0.0.1-rc.1 -R integrio-intropy/intropy-cli --yes --cleanup-tag
git tag -d v0.0.1-rc.1
# remove the rc cask from the tap so it doesn't linger
gh api -X DELETE repos/integrio-intropy/homebrew-tap/contents/Casks/intropy.rb -f message="remove rc test cask" -f sha="$(gh api repos/integrio-intropy/homebrew-tap/contents/Casks/intropy.rb --jq .sha)"
```

Then for launch: make both repos public → `git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0` → publish the draft release.

---

Pushing the tag kicks off a real CI run that writes to the tap, so I'll let you trigger it (or say the word and I'll create and push `v0.0.1-rc.1` and watch the run for you). Want me to drive it?

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy
    - go test ./...

builds:
  - id: intropy
    main: ./cmd/intropy
    binary: intropy
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - linux
      - darwin
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X main.version={{.Version}}
      - -X main.commit={{.Commit}}
      - -X main.date={{.Date}}
    flags:
      - -trimpath

archives:
  - formats: [tar.gz]
    name_template: >-
      {{ .ProjectName }}_
      {{- .Version }}_
      {{- .Os }}_
      {{- .Arch }}
    files:
      - README.md
      - LICENSE
      - CONTRIBUTING.md
      - install.sh

signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    certificate: '${artifact}.pem'
    args:
      - sign-blob
      - '--output-certificate=${certificate}'
      - '--output-signature=${signature}'
      - '${artifact}'
    artifacts: all

checksum:
  name_template: checksums.txt
  algorithm: sha256

snapshot:
  version_template: "{{ incpatch .Version }}-rc"

changelog:
  sort: asc
  use: github
  filters:
    exclude:
      - '^docs:'
      - '^test:'
      - '^chore:'
      - Merge pull request
      - Merge branch
  groups:
    - title: Features
      regexp: '^.*?feat(\(.+\))?!?:.*$'
      order: 0
    - title: Bug Fixes
      regexp: '^.*?fix(\(.+\))?!?:.*$'
      order: 1
    - title: Other Changes
      order: 999

homebrew_casks:
  - name: intropy
    repository:
      owner: integrio-intropy
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli"
    description: "CLI for Intropy integrations"
    generate_completions_from_executable:
      executable: intropy
      args:
        - completion
      shells:
        - bash
        - zsh
        - fish
    # The binary is signed with cosign (sigstore), not Apple-notarized, so macOS
    # Gatekeeper would quarantine it. Strip the quarantine attribute on install.
    hooks:
      post:
        install: |
          if OS.mac?
            system_command "/usr/bin/xattr", args: ["-dr", "com.apple.quarantine", "#{staged_path}/intropy"]
          end

release:
  github:
    owner: integrio-intropy
    name: intropy-cli
  draft: true
  prerelease: auto
  extra_files:
    - glob: ./install.sh

content.text:
Found it — it's the only `intropy` on your PATH:

```
/Users/robinhultman/go/bin/intropy   (16 MB, from `go install`)
```

Just delete that file:

```sh
rm /Users/robinhultman/go/bin/intropy
```

That's all `go install` leaves behind — there's no package manifest to clean up.

A couple of notes:
- **PATH ordering is in your favor.** `~/go/bin` currently shadows everything, and Homebrew installs to `/opt/homebrew/bin`. Once you remove the Go binary and `brew install`, `which intropy` will resolve to `/opt/homebrew/bin/intropy`.
- **Clear your shell's command cache** after switching, or your current zsh session may still point at the old path:
  ```sh
  hash -r          # (or: rehash)
  which intropy    # should show /opt/homebrew/bin/intropy after brew install
  ```

You can do this removal anytime before or after `brew install` — if both exist at once, `~/go/bin` would win until you remove it, so removing it is what makes the Homebrew one take over.

Want me to run the `rm` for you? (It may prompt for confirmation since it's a delete.)

# intropy CLI

`intropy` is the command-line interface for working with Intropy integrations.
It **scaffolds integrations** from the official Intropy blueprint library hosted at
[`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints).

## Install

### Homebrew (macOS)

Distributed as a Homebrew cask (macOS only):

```sh
brew install integrio-intropy/tap/intropy
```

On Linux, use the quick install script below or download a binary from the
[releases page](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli/releases).

### Quick install (macOS / Linux)

```sh
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh
```

With options:

```sh
# Install to a custom prefix
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --prefix ~/.local

# Install a specific version
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.1.0
```

The script detects your OS and architecture, downloads the matching release
archive, verifies the SHA256 checksum, optionally verifies the cosign signature,
and installs the binary and shell completions.

### From source

Requires Go 1.26+.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli.git
cd intropy-cli
make build
```

Or manually:

```sh
go build -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
```

Add `bin/` to your `PATH`, or move the binary somewhere on your `PATH`.

### Verifying signatures

Release binaries are signed with [cosign](https://sigstore.dev/) using
keyless signing via GitHub Actions OIDC. Each release includes `.sig` and
`.pem` files for every archive.

```sh
# Download the archive, its .sig, and its .pem from the GitHub release
cosign verify-blob \
  --certificate intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.pem \
  --signature intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.sig \
  --certificate-identity-regexp="https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
```

### Windows

Windows is not a supported native target. Install and run `intropy` inside
[WSL 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) using the Linux
instructions above. The CLI relies on Unix path conventions and signal handling
that are not tested on Windows.

### Version stamping

Version, commit, and build date are injected via `-ldflags` at release time:

```sh
go build -ldflags "\
  -X main.version=$(git describe --tags --always) \
  -X main.commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
  -X main.date=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
  -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
```

Check what you have with:

```sh
intropy version
```

## Quickstart

### Scaffold your first integration

```sh
# Inspect a blueprint before you scaffold it
intropy int describe hello-world

# Render it into a new directory
intropy int create hello-world -o ./my-integration
```

## Command overview

```
intropy
├── int                    Manage integrations
│   ├── create <blueprint>     Scaffold a new integration from a blueprint
│   └── describe <blueprint>   Print a blueprint's manifest and parameter schema
└── version                Print version information
```

Run any command with `--help` for full flag documentation.

## Integrations (`intropy int`)

### Describe a blueprint

Inspect what parameters a blueprint accepts before scaffolding it:

```sh
intropy int describe hello-world
intropy int describe hello-world --version v1.2.0
intropy int describe hello-world -o json   # machine-readable; same schema Backstage renders
```

Without `--version`, the latest GitHub release is used.

### Create an integration

```sh
intropy int create hello-world --output ./my-integration
```

Provide parameter values inline, from files, or interactively:

```sh
# inline
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --set name=orders --set owner=team-x

# from a values file (repeatable; use - for stdin)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out -f values.yaml

# disable interactive prompts (fail fast on missing required values)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --no-input -f values.yaml

# write a machine-readable result document (consumed by chained scaffolders)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --output-json result.json
```

Use `--force` to render into a non-empty directory.

## Project layout

```
cmd/intropy/         Cobra command wiring (one file per command)
internal/blueprint/  Blueprint download, validation, describe, render
```

## Exit codes

- `0` — success
- `1` — runtime error
- `2` — usage error (unknown command, missing required flag, bad argument)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `intropy int create` fails with "blueprint not found" | The blueprint name is misspelled or does not exist in the library. | Run `intropy int describe <name>` to verify the blueprint exists. Check spelling and case. |
| Windows native errors | Running the Linux binary directly on Windows without WSL. | Use WSL 2 — native Windows is not supported. |

For issues not listed here, run the failing command with `--help` to verify flag usage, or open an issue with the output of `intropy version` and the exact command you ran.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for build instructions, code standards,
and the pull request workflow.

## References

- [`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints)
  — the blueprint library `intropy int create` and `intropy int describe`
  download from by default.

# intropy CLI

`intropy` is the command-line interface for working with Intropy integrations.
It **scaffolds integrations** from the official Intropy blueprint library hosted at
[`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints).

## Install

### Homebrew (macOS)

Distributed as a Homebrew cask (macOS only):

```sh
brew tap integrio-intropy/tap
brew trust --tap integrio-intropy/tap
brew install intropy
```

The `brew trust` step is required when `HOMEBREW_REQUIRE_TAP_TRUST` is set —
the default on current Homebrew (6.x+). On older versions without that
requirement you can skip it.

On Linux, use the quick install script below or download a binary from the
[releases page](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli/releases).

### Quick install (macOS / Linux)

```sh
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh
```

With options:

```sh
# Install to a custom prefix
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --prefix ~/.local

# Install a specific version
curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.1.0
```

The script detects your OS and architecture, downloads the matching release
archive, verifies the SHA256 checksum, optionally verifies the cosign signature,
and installs the binary and shell completions.

### From source

Requires Go 1.26+.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli.git
cd intropy-cli
make build
```

Or manually:

```sh
go build -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
```

Add `bin/` to your `PATH`, or move the binary somewhere on your `PATH`.

### Verifying signatures

Release binaries are signed with [cosign](https://sigstore.dev/) using
keyless signing via GitHub Actions OIDC. Each release includes `.sig` and
`.pem` files for every archive.

```sh
# Download the archive, its .sig, and its .pem from the GitHub release
cosign verify-blob \
  --certificate intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.pem \
  --signature intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz.sig \
  --certificate-identity-regexp="https://github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  intropy_Darwin_arm64.tar.gz
```

### Windows

Windows is not a supported native target. Install and run `intropy` inside
[WSL 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) using the Linux
instructions above. The CLI relies on Unix path conventions and signal handling
that are not tested on Windows.

### Version stamping

Version, commit, and build date are injected via `-ldflags` at release time:

```sh
go build -ldflags "\
  -X main.version=$(git describe --tags --always) \
  -X main.commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
  -X main.date=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
  -o bin/intropy ./cmd/intropy
```

Check what you have with:

```sh
intropy version
```

## Quickstart

### Scaffold your first integration

```sh
# Inspect a blueprint before you scaffold it
intropy int describe hello-world

# Render it into a new directory
intropy int create hello-world -o ./my-integration
```

## Command overview

```
intropy
├── int                    Manage integrations
│   ├── create <blueprint>     Scaffold a new integration from a blueprint
│   └── describe <blueprint>   Print a blueprint's manifest and parameter schema
└── version                Print version information
```

Run any command with `--help` for full flag documentation.

## Integrations (`intropy int`)

### Describe a blueprint

Inspect what parameters a blueprint accepts before scaffolding it:

```sh
intropy int describe hello-world
intropy int describe hello-world --version v1.2.0
intropy int describe hello-world -o json   # machine-readable; same schema Backstage renders
```

Without `--version`, the latest GitHub release is used.

### Create an integration

```sh
intropy int create hello-world --output ./my-integration
```

Provide parameter values inline, from files, or interactively:

```sh
# inline
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --set name=orders --set owner=team-x

# from a values file (repeatable; use - for stdin)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out -f values.yaml

# disable interactive prompts (fail fast on missing required values)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --no-input -f values.yaml

# write a machine-readable result document (consumed by chained scaffolders)
intropy int create hello-world -o ./out --output-json result.json
```

Use `--force` to render into a non-empty directory.

## Project layout

```
cmd/intropy/         Cobra command wiring (one file per command)
internal/blueprint/  Blueprint download, validation, describe, render
```

## Exit codes

- `0` — success
- `1` — runtime error
- `2` — usage error (unknown command, missing required flag, bad argument)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `intropy int create` fails with "blueprint not found" | The blueprint name is misspelled or does not exist in the library. | Run `intropy int describe <name>` to verify the blueprint exists. Check spelling and case. |
| Windows native errors | Running the Linux binary directly on Windows without WSL. | Use WSL 2 — native Windows is not supported. |

For issues not listed here, run the failing command with `--help` to verify flag usage, or open an issue with the output of `intropy version` and the exact command you ran.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for build instructions, code standards,
and the pull request workflow.

## References

- [`integrio-intropy/blueprints`](https://github.com/integrio-intropy/blueprints)
  — the blueprint library `intropy int create` and `intropy int describe`
  download from by default.

#!/bin/sh
# install.sh — install intropy from GitHub Releases
#
# Usage:
#   curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh
#   curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.1.0
#   curl -fsSL https://get.intropy.example/install.sh | sh -s -- --prefix ~/.local

set -e

OWNER="integrio-intropy"
REPO="intropy-cli"
BINARY="intropy"
GITHUB="https://github.com/${OWNER}/${REPO}"

# Defaults
PREFIX=""
VERSION=""

# Parse arguments passed via sh -s -- ...
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
	case "$1" in
		--version)
			VERSION="$2"
			shift 2
			;;
		--prefix)
			PREFIX="$2"
			shift 2
			;;
		-h|--help)
			echo "Usage: install.sh [--version VERSION] [--prefix PREFIX]"
			echo ""
			echo "Options:"
			echo "  --version VERSION   Install a specific version (default: latest)"
			echo "  --prefix PREFIX     Install directory (default: /usr/local/bin or ~/.local/bin)"
			exit 0
			;;
		*)
			echo "Unknown option: $1"
			exit 1
			;;
	esac
done

# --- detect OS ---
OS=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
case "$OS" in
	linux) OS="Linux" ;;
	darwin) OS="Darwin" ;;
	*)
		echo "Unsupported operating system: $OS"
		echo "Supported: Linux, Darwin (macOS)"
		exit 1
		;;
esac

# --- detect architecture ---
ARCH=$(uname -m)
case "$ARCH" in
	x86_64) ARCH="amd64" ;;
	aarch64|arm64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
	*)
		echo "Unsupported architecture: $ARCH"
		echo "Supported: amd64, arm64"
		exit 1
		;;
esac

# --- resolve version ---
if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
	# Fetch the latest release tag from GitHub API
	echo "==> Resolving latest version..."
	VERSION=$(curl -fsSL "${GITHUB}/releases/latest" | sed -n 's/.*tag_name":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
	if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
		echo "Failed to determine latest version"
		exit 1
	fi
fi

echo "==> Installing ${BINARY} ${VERSION} for ${OS}/${ARCH}..."

# --- determine install directory ---
if [ -z "$PREFIX" ]; then
	# Try /usr/local/bin first, fall back to ~/.local/bin
	if [ -w "/usr/local/bin" ] 2>/dev/null || mkdir -p "/usr/local/bin" 2>/dev/null; then
		PREFIX="/usr/local/bin"
	else
		PREFIX="${HOME}/.local/bin"
		mkdir -p "$PREFIX"
	fi
fi

if [ ! -d "$PREFIX" ]; then
	mkdir -p "$PREFIX" || {
		echo "Failed to create directory: $PREFIX"
		exit 1
	}
fi

echo "==> Install directory: $PREFIX"

# --- download artifact ---
ARTIFACT="${BINARY}_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR"' EXIT

BASE_URL="${GITHUB}/releases/download/${VERSION}"

echo "==> Downloading ${ARTIFACT}..."
curl -fsSL "${BASE_URL}/${ARTIFACT}" -o "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}"

# --- download and verify checksum ---
echo "==> Verifying checksum..."
curl -fsSL "${BASE_URL}/checksums.txt" -o "${TMPDIR}/checksums.txt"
cd "$TMPDIR"

# Extract the expected checksum for our artifact
EXPECTED=$(grep "${ARTIFACT}" checksums.txt | awk '{print $1}')
if [ -z "$EXPECTED" ]; then
	echo "Artifact not found in checksums.txt"
	exit 1
fi

# Compute actual checksum
ACTUAL=$(sha256sum "${ARTIFACT}" | awk '{print $1}')
if [ "$EXPECTED" != "$ACTUAL" ]; then
	echo "Checksum mismatch!"
	echo "  expected: ${EXPECTED}"
	echo "  actual:   ${ACTUAL}"
	exit 1
fi

echo "==> Checksum OK"

# --- optional cosign verification ---
if command -v cosign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo "==> Verifying signature with cosign..."
	curl -fsSL "${BASE_URL}/${ARTIFACT}.sig" -o "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}.sig"
	curl -fsSL "${BASE_URL}/${ARTIFACT}.pem" -o "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}.pem"
	cosign verify-blob \
		--certificate "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}.pem" \
		--signature "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}.sig" \
		--certificate-identity-regexp="https://github.com/${OWNER}/${REPO}" \
		--certificate-oidc-issuer="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
		"${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}" || {
		echo "Cosign verification failed"
		exit 1
	}
	echo "==> Signature verified"
else
	echo "==> cosign not found, skipping signature verification"
	echo "    (install cosign to verify: https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/installation/)"
fi

# --- extract and install ---
echo "==> Extracting..."
tar -xzf "${TMPDIR}/${ARTIFACT}" -C "$TMPDIR"

# The binary should be at TMPDIR/intropy or TMPDIR/bin/intropy
if [ -f "${TMPDIR}/${BINARY}" ]; then
	BINARY_PATH="${TMPDIR}/${BINARY}"
elif [ -f "${TMPDIR}/bin/${BINARY}" ]; then
	BINARY_PATH="${TMPDIR}/bin/${BINARY}"
else
	echo "Binary not found in archive"
	exit 1
fi

echo "==> Installing ${BINARY} to ${PREFIX}..."
if [ -w "$PREFIX" ]; then
	install -m 755 "$BINARY_PATH" "${PREFIX}/${BINARY}"
else
	echo "    (sudo required for ${PREFIX})"
	sudo install -m 755 "$BINARY_PATH" "${PREFIX}/${BINARY}"
fi

# --- install shell completions ---
if command -v "${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo "==> Installing shell completions..."

	# Bash
	if [ -d "/etc/bash_completion.d" ] && [ -w "/etc/bash_completion.d" ]; then
		"${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" completion bash > "/etc/bash_completion.d/${BINARY}"
		echo "    bash: /etc/bash_completion.d/${BINARY}"
	elif [ -d "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d" ] && [ -w "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d" ]; then
		"${PREFIX}/${BINARY}" completion bash > "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/${BINARY}"
